links.outcome: Failure modes identified by multidisciplinary FMEA of AI planning workflow and risk after mitigation
links.effect: 39 failure modes identified: 33 Acceptable, five Tolerable, one Not acceptable; after mitigation two Tolerable and none Not acceptable.
links.quote: Of these, 33 were ‘Acceptable’, five ‘Tolerable’, and one ‘Not acceptable’ according to the risk matrix (see Fig. 3 and Table 3 ).

links.outcome: Documented risk assessment with scores updated after corrective actions across the workflow
links.effect: Risk scores re-evaluated after corrective actions; risk reduced to two Tolerable failure modes and none Not acceptable.
links.quote: When a corrective action was identified, its effectiveness was re-evaluated, and the risk scores were updated.

links.outcome: Case-specific QA flagging out-of-training-distribution inputs, effect on detectability of bad predictions
links.effect: Case-specific QA report lowered lack-of-detectability score for 'prediction is bad' (8.17 to 3.51 risk score, Tolerable to Acceptable); residual ~3% risk dosimetrist overlooks report.
links.quote: The case-specific QA report was chosen as a barrier against the ‘prediction is bad’ failure mode (see Table 3 ), which decreased the lack of detectability score.

links.outcome: Output analysis of CNN MLC/MU predictions against validation/test distributions to detect anomalous predictions
links.effect: QA report outputs metrics (AAV, LSV, MU) compared with validation/test data; risk of bad prediction reduced to Acceptable, though implementation not done and estimated only.
links.quote: Metrics such as Aperture Area Variability (AAV) and Leaf Sequence Variability (LSV) [16] , [17] per arc could assess the complexity of MLC movements, while total MU and its standard deviation per arc could gauge MU consistency.

models_evaluated: In-house CNN-based breast VMAT autoplanning tool

links.effect: 39 failure modes were identified and classified as 33 ‘Acceptable’, five ‘Tolerable’, and one ‘Not acceptable’.
links.quote: Of these, 33 were ‘Acceptable’, five ‘Tolerable’, and one ‘Not acceptable’ according to the risk matrix (see Fig. 3 and Table 3 ).

links.effect: Outside-training-range bad prediction: S=4, O=7, D=8.17; risk classified Tolerable.
links.quote: Detailed in Table 3 , one ‘Tolerable’ failure mode was bad predictions by the DL model for atypical cases, such as patients with unusually large breast volumes or changes in CT scanner specifications.

links.effect: Case-specific QA lowered lack-of-detectability from 8.17 to 3.51 and risk from Tolerable to Acceptable.
links.quote: The case-specific QA report was chosen as a barrier against the ‘prediction is bad’ failure mode (see Table 3 ), which decreased the lack of detectability score.

links.effect: For three optimization-setting failures, occurrence dropped from 8.33 to 3.79; all moved to Acceptable.
links.quote: A pop-up to remind the dosimetrist to adapt the multiresolution level, the aperture shape controller, the optimisation mode and intermediate dose calculation before optimisation, decreased the occurrence score of these failure modes, moving them into the ‘Acceptable’ zone of the risk matrix.

links.effect: Before mitigation, de-pseudonymisation with wrong patient data had S=7, O=1, D=8.17; risk classified Tolerable.
links.quote: Another failure involved the de-pseudonymisation of data due to an error, swapping meta information with another patient’s.
